doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Miles Davis band and Kind of Blue
title: Van Gelder's studio and Coltrane sessions
summary: Cobb explains how he played alternate on Rudy Van Gelder dates.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Parallel with – and particularly, I think, when you got to Europe with the things you were doing – Miles – you end up doing some things with Trane. I don’t know whether they were intended to be recordings or what, but things you did in Europe. Do
you have any recollection of just the recordings that you did with Trane out while you were with Miles, outside of working – recording with Miles?
There was a thing where this guy had a studio in New Jersey. It was . . .

He had a studio over there. Every Sunday – actually, the studio was at his mother’s living room. They made – he made a studio in his mother’s living room. That’s how he started. They used to go over there every Saturday and make records, anybody. Mostly they used Miles’s band. They used Paul and Joe and Red and Trane. So Trane used to make – bring people over every week, and they’d make a different record. When Joe couldn’t make it, they used alternate people. They had alternate person to go, each instrument. So I got into the flow there some kind of way. When Joe couldn’t make some stuff, I would probably do it or another alternate would do it. That’s how I got to make some records with Trane over there.
